user_equation_group.interpretation: The three images are one equation group, not two independent equations. The simulation generalizes the fixed 0,1 to epsilon_n=0,1^n=10^-n. Thus gamma_n=1/epsilon_n=10^n. Modern Turkish short-scale nonilyon=10^30, so the gamma coefficient reaches one nonillion at n=30. The literal alternative n=10^30 is recorded only in logarithmic form (log10 gamma=10^30); it is not iterated step by step.

reference_ship.basis: Exp28/Exp34 reference mission. Exp34 In knee exhaust speed 44.81 km/s (Isp 4570 s, F/P 39.9 µN/W) and In 5 kV exhaust speed about 91.7 km/s from the same 10/8 kg mass ratio. Photon exhaust u=c is a lower-bound comparison, not an Exp34 operating point.

simulation_space.ladder: Continuous and integer n=0..30; epsilon=10^-n, gamma=10^n, beta=sqrt(1-epsilon^2), rapidity=acosh(gamma). For n>=8, 1-beta is computed as epsilon^2/(1+beta) to avoid floating-point cancellation.
lanes: onboard ion rocket: relativistic rocket mass ratio R=exp((c/u)*rapidity) for Exp34 exhaust speeds
photon rocket lower bound: u=c, R=exp(rapidity)
ideal external-energy ladder: kinetic energy (gamma-1)*m_dry*c^2 and supply time at 100 W
frequency lane: per-In-ion nu=gamma*m_In*c^2/h and lambda=h/(gamma*m_In*c)
negative branch audit: E_-=-gamma*m0*c^2 gives m0*c^2/E_-=-10^-n, so it cannot equal +0,1^n for positive m0 and positive frequency without redefining E or nu
gravitational analogue only: epsilon_g=sqrt(1-r_s/r), hence r/r_s=1/(1-epsilon^2); f(r_s) is not defined in the images, so this is labelled an analogue, not a derived ship drive

predictions: D1 LADDER: n=1 gives gamma=10 and beta=0,9949874371 (1-beta=5,0126e-3). n=30 gives gamma=1,0e30 (one nonillion) and 1-beta=5,0e-61 within 1%.
